final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrowing is analytically useful, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the unresolved item is not merely a cautionary note; it is a policy predicate. The available evidence shows a named launch use case tied to customer commitments, an evaluation gap in that segment, an open legal question about disclosure, and a policy requiring disclosure of material limitations unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The Actor expressly concedes that the current record does not show disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance. On this record, certification now remains unsupported as compliant, even if aggregate launch readiness is otherwise defensible.
remaining_concerns: The insurance claims triage segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points and is named in two carrier pilot commitments, making the weakness plausibly material under the stated policy.
The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The record still does not show disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed remains open, so a required compliance predicate is unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness only; they do not satisfy the separate disclosure requirement.
